output.reason: The brief is persuasive. The RFI audit trail undermines the late-information claim, and moving the crane looks like a decision Callerby made for itself. But the brief admits it never tested whether CO-09 really held up the frame, and that is the core of the 17-week claim. It also takes the Kestrel incentive link less seriously than it deserves: the crane went to Kestrel, Kestrel handed over seven weeks early, and the incentive paid out to the team Gareth agreed the move with.
